source.question: why did F-15 D drop off so much in its second year

submission.summary: F-15 D made about 19% less oil in its second calendar year than its first, most likely because its natural decline is steep and water arrived early. It averaged about 68,100 Sm3 in 2014 and about 55,100 Sm3 in 2015, with liquid rate steady and the choke unchanged, while water cut rose from near zero to 51% by December 2015.

findings.claim: F-15 D produced about 68,100 Sm3 in 2014 and about 55,100 Sm3 in 2015, about 19% less year-on-year.
findings.detail: Yearly totals from production_daily: 2014 oil 68,136 Sm3, 2015 oil 55,099 Sm3; ratio 0.8087 = -19.1%.

findings.claim: Its oil rate was already falling before water arrived, averaging 33% less after around 2014-08-03 than before, 270 Sm3/d to 182 Sm3/d with choke unchanged.
findings.detail: Regime change oil_rate around 2014-08-03: before_mean 270.29 -> after_mean 182.15 Sm3/d, relative_change -0.3261; change across 4 weeks -15%; choke 12% -> 11%, choke_moved false. Harmonic decline fit on 2014-01-16 to 2015-07-18: qi 332.07 Sm3/d, di 1.04 per year, r2_log 0.7935, no warnings.

findings.claim: Water broke through in its second year, with 30-day median water cut above 5% on 2015-02-20 and a shift to an average water cut of 50% after around 2015-08-23.
findings.detail: Threshold crossing 0.05 on 2015-02-20, 13 months after first oil; regime change water_cut around 2015-08-23: before_mean 0.03169 -> after_mean 0.4966 (+0.4649), across 0.08273 -> 0.3531. By_year water cut 0% in 2014, 7.5% in 2015, 56% in 2016. Liquid rate 233 Sm3/d in 2014 to 196 Sm3/d in 2015, choke 11.5% to 10.3%.

findings.claim: A workover in August 2015 added four new perforated intervals and lifted oil rate in August to September 2015, but water kept rising to 51% by December 2015.
findings.detail: Workover 2015-08-05 to 2015-08-16: perforations 3748-3766 mMD, 3540-3552 mMD, 3508-3517 mMD, 3483-3491 mMD. Monthly oil rate per producing day 128 Sm3/d in July 2015 -> 311 Sm3/d in August 2015 -> 248 Sm3/d in September 2015; water cut 7.6% -> 34% -> 35% -> 51% in Dec 2015. Field voidage replacement near 1.0 in 2014 and 2015, so injection kept pace.

result.summary: oil_rate shifts around 2014-08-03: weekly mean 270 -> 182 (-33%) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 226 -> 191 (-15%); the choke stayed about the same (12 -> 11%).
Shut in for 13 days from 2014-08-20. Oil rate 195 -> 197 Sm3/d (+1%) after restart. Same time as F-1 C; F-11, F-12, F-14 kept flowing.
Shut in for 36 days from 2014-11-26. Oil rate 190 -> 211 Sm3/d (+11%) after restart. Same time as F-1 C, F-12; F-11, F-14 kept flowing.
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.05 on 2015-02-20, 13 months after first oil.
Shut in for 27 days from 2015-07-19. Oil rate 126 -> 289 Sm3/d (+129%) after restart. Same time as F-1 C; F-11, F-12, F-14 kept flowing.
water_cut shifts around 2015-08-23: weekly mean 0.0317 -> 0.497 (+0.46) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.08 -> 0.35 (+0.27).
Shut in for 16 days from 2015-11-23. Oil rate 208 -> 200 Sm3/d (-4%) after restart. Same time as F-1 C; F-11, F-12, F-14 kept flowing.
Shut in for 15 days from 2016-01-05. Oil rate 200 -> 189 Sm3/d (-5%) after restart. Same time as F-1 C; F-11, F-12, F-14 kept flowing.
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.5 on 2016-02-04, 25 months after first oil.
Shut in for 12 days from 2016-03-25. Oil rate 167 -> 192 Sm3/d (+15%) after restart. Same time as F-1 C; F-11, F-12, F-14 kept flowing.
Shut in for 73 days from 2016-07-07. Same time as F-12, F-14, F-5; F-11 kept flowing.

result.no_trend: too few months with WOR >= 1 (water cut 0.5) to fit a trend: 8, need 12
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. The water cuts in to_limits are reference points, not an economic limit: the data holds no costs or prices, so remaining_oil_sm3 says how much oil is left before each, not whether it pays. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

result.note: Daily reports exist for drilling and for work on the well (wireline, plugs, perforations, production logs), not for days of normal production. A job's date is the day the work was done; kind is drilling, completion, workover (work on a producing or injecting well) or abandonment. Ask for one day to see every operation line.

issues.text: oil rate 60% lower in the period after than before (weekly mean 1,259 -> 509 Sm3/d), a gradual change: 23% across it

result.levels: alarm: act now; caution: watch; note: for the record

arguments.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', date) AS yr, SUM(oil_sm3) AS oil, SUM(water_sm3) AS water, AVG(water_cut) AS wc, AVG(CASE WHEN on_stream_hrs>0 THEN oil_sm3/NULLIF(on_stream_hrs/24.0,0) END) AS rate FROM production_daily WHERE well='F-15 D' GROUP BY yr ORDER BY yr
